findings.obs_text: Where the word is attention set on a matter, live and dead name the state it reaches: in Isa 53:8 who considered that he was cut off from the land of the living, in Eze 18:28 the one who considered and turned shall live, in Rom 4:19 Abraham considered his body as good as dead, in Heb 11:19 he considered God able to raise from the dead. In 2Ki 3:14 lives is the Lord of the oath and regard is Elisha's regard for the king.
findings.grounds: he considered that God was able even to raise him

older.finding: A body "as good as dead", and faith that considers it.
older.reason: it states how live works in a person; the live collection owns it

older.finding: Face: D24. Like the dead; Hits / verses: 12 / 12; What differs: The living likened to the dead; the heart that died; "dead dog"; Example verses: Psa 88:5; 143:3; 1Sa 25:37; 2Sa 9:8; Rom 4:19
older.reason: it states a face or use of the live words; the live collection owns it

older.finding: "Put to death" (H4191 hiphil, G3499) is used of executing a person (Num 35) and of "what is earthly in you" (Col 3:5). The same Greek root gives a body "as good as dead" (Rom 4:19; Heb 11:12). *(R: noted as the range of the word. No verse sets these side by side.)*
older.reason: it states how live works in a person; the live collection owns it

older.finding: G6. Like the dead.: The guards "became like dead men" for fear (Mat 28:4).; John "fell at his feet as though dead" (Rev 1:17).; Abraham's body "as good as dead" (Rom 4:19).
older.reason: it states how live works in a person; the live collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Job 9:21 regard not and loathe stand together of Job's own self: he does not regard himself and loathes his life. In Lam 4:2 regarded as earthen pots stands against precious sons, worth their weight in gold: counting low set against valued. In Jos 7:21 weighing is the weight of the gold bar, beside coveted.
findings.grounds: I regard not myself; I loathe my life

older.finding: Other texts where the soul turns against its own life: "I loathe my life; I will give free utterance to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul" (Job 10:1; 9:21)
older.reason: it states how love works in a person; the love collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Heb 11:11 Sarah considered him faithful who had promised, and in 1Pe 5:12 Peter regards Silvanus as a faithful brother: the counting names faithfulness as its value. In Job 35:13 and Eze 18:28 surely is an emphasis on what God does not regard and on the one who shall live, not loyalty.
findings.grounds: since she considered him faithful who had promised

findings.obs_text: In Dan 7:8 great things are spoken by the little horn that Daniel considered: the considering is set on the horn, the great things are its boasting.
findings.grounds: I considered the horns, and behold

findings.obs_text: In Pro 17:28 the fool who keeps silent is considered wise: silence is the ground on which others count him wise. In Job 2:3 still is Job holding fast his integrity, and in Isa 33:8 the traveler ceases where there is no regard for man: neither is silence of speech.
findings.grounds: Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise

older.finding: Being silent is a person's, or God's, holding back of speech for a reason the verse shows: submission, fear, shame, awe, wisdom, obedience, waiting, or failure to speak up; or the refusal of it (anguish, praise, the watchmen's duty).
older.reason: it states a face or use of the mute words; the mute collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In 2Ch 5:11 the priests there had all consecrated themselves, not keeping to their divisions: regard is keeping to an order, present is being there; neither offers.
In Isa 53:8 oppression is what took the servant away, and the question is who of his generation considered it: the considering is of what was done to him by oppression.
findings.grounds: By oppression and judgment he was taken away

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 5:12 Peter regards Silvanus as faithful and, by him, writes exhorting and declaring: the regard of the writer for the carrier stands beside the preaching of the letter.
findings.grounds: exhorting and declaring that this is the true grace

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 1:16 Hannah asks Eli not to regard her as a worthless woman, and in 1Sa 25:25 Abigail asks David not to regard Nabal: regarding is counting a person as worthless. In Job 37:24 God does not regard the wise in their own conceit: conceit is what he withholds regard from. In Ecc 2:11 the Preacher considered all his toil, and it was vanity.
findings.grounds: Do not regard your servant as a worthless woman

older.finding: "Vanity and a striving after wind" (*hevel* + *rûaḥ*): Ecc 1:14; 2:11, 17, 26; 4:4, 16; 6:9.
older.reason: it states how pride works in a person; the pride collection owns it

older.finding: 1.9 ◆ Desire aimed at wind: "all is vanity and a striving after wind" (Ecc 1:14; 2:11, 17, 26; 4:4, 6)
older.reason: it states how pride works in a person; the pride collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Heb 11:11 the one Sarah considered faithful is the one who had promised: the counting rests on the promise.
findings.grounds: since she considered him faithful who had promised

findings.obs_text: In Luk 22:24 the disciples dispute over who among them should be counted the greatest: being regarded is the prize the dispute is about.
findings.grounds: which of them was to be regarded as the greatest

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 5:12 true names the grace Peter declares; regard is his counting of Silvanus as faithful: the two stand in one verse without joining.
findings.grounds: this is the true grace of God
